placementAdvice.text: The title stays fixed 8 px above the content, and the items in the slot are 8 px apart, as in Figma.

configuration.text: pinToBottom is on by default: the sheet is pinned to the bottom of its parent, absolute and full width. Set it to false to render the sheet in normal flow, inside your own layout container.

safeAreaBottom is on by default: it adds the device's bottom safe-area inset (home indicator) on top of the sheet's bottom padding, so content stays clear of the indicator when the sheet rests at the bottom of the screen.

examples.purpose: Choosing how to pay, the guide's In context, with the sheet shown: the payment screen (a line of Text and its Change payment method Button) is dimmed by a bare Overlay, and the sheet titled “Pay with” docks to the bottom over it, holding the three payment options as List Items in a ListGroup. visible stands for the screen's shown state, which the Button's onPress sets; a row's onPress stands for keeping that choice and hiding the sheet, and the Overlay's onPress for hiding it on a tap on the dimmed screen. The screen renders the Overlay only while the sheet shows.
examples.jsx:
<Screen>
  <Text>Pay ₹500 to Asha Stores</Text>
  <Button label="Change payment method" onPress={() => {}} />
  <Overlay onPress={() => {}} />
  <ContentSheet visible title="Pay with">
    <ListGroup>
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="UPI" supportText="Jio Payments Bank •• 4821" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Debit card" supportText="•• 9012" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Net banking" supportText="Any bank" onPress={() => {}} />
    </ListGroup>
  </ContentSheet>
</Screen>

from.quote: Choosing an option, or tapping the dimmed screen, closes it; the screen keeps the choice.

examples.purpose: The same payment screen with the sheet hidden, as after a choice: visible={false} and no Overlay, so only the screen shows; the sheet waits below the screen, out of the Tab order and hidden from screen readers. The Button's onPress stands for the screen showing the sheet (and its Overlay) again.

props.name: children
props.description: Sheet content. The sheet is one big slot: whatever you place here is stacked in a column (separated by the `contentSheet/gap` token) inside the sheet's padding. The sheet has **no fixed height** — it grows and shrinks to fit these children automatically.

props.name: modes
props.description: Design-token modes. Cascaded to every slot child via {@link cloneChildrenWithModes} so nested `ListItem`/`Section`/etc. resolve the same theme without you wiring `modes` onto each one.

props.name: title
props.description: On the web the title is a centred h1 (role heading) in a fixed header outside the scroller, so it stays put while the content scrolls; each titled sheet adds a page heading. Declared: Optional title rendered in a centered, sticky header at the top of the sheet. Uses the same `drawer/title*` token family as the `Drawer` title so the two surfaces stay visually consistent.

props.name: avoidKeyboard
props.description: Deprecated: Keyboard avoidance is now owned by the consuming implementation. This prop is retained for backwards compatibility, defaults to `false`, and has no effect. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: keyboardSpacing
props.description: Deprecated: Keyboard avoidance is now owned by the consuming implementation. This prop is retained for backwards compatibility and has no effect. Default 0, from the component source.

props.name: safeAreaBottom
props.description: Add the device's bottom safe-area inset (home indicator) on top of the sheet's bottom padding, so content never sits under the indicator when the sheet rests at the bottom of the screen. Default `true`. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: pinToBottom
props.description: Not a portal or modal: pinned, the sheet is absolute at left, right and bottom 0 inside its nearest positioned parent (full width, flush bottom); pinToBottom={false} puts it in normal flow. Declared: Pin the sheet to the bottom of its parent (absolute, full width). This is the default behaviour — the sheet "just stays at the bottom". Set to `false` to render the sheet in normal flow instead (e.g. when you compose it inside your own layout container). Default true, from the component source.

props.name: visible
props.description: A hidden sheet stays mounted; on the web it is inert and aria-hidden, with its controls at tabindex -1, so Tab skips it and screen readers don't read it. Declared: Controls whether the sheet is on-screen. When this becomes `true` the sheet springs up from the bottom edge (off-screen → on-screen) using the same spring as the {@link Drawer} (`damping: 32`, `stiffness: 300`); when it becomes `false` it springs back down below the bottom edge. The sheet pops up on mount by default. The animation runs entirely on the UI thread via `react-native-reanimated` (no re-renders). Default `true`. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: maxHeightPercent
props.description: The maximum height is maxHeightPercent of the parent's height (448 px in a 640 px parent at the default 0.7); past it the content scrolls, with the scrollbar hidden. Declared: Max height of the sheet as a fraction (0–1) of the parent height (measured with `onLayout` when the sheet is pinned). When content reaches this height the slot scrolls and the title stays fixed. Default `0.7`. Default 0.7, from the component source.

props.name: style
props.description: Optional style override applied to the sheet container.

props.name: ...Omit<ViewProps, 'style' | 'children'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection ContentSheet reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Page type
modes.description: MainPage and SubPage give a white sheet (#ffffff), JioPlus a light grey one (#f5f5f5). Declared: A token collection ContentSheet reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Sheet content. The sheet is one big slot: whatever you place here is stacked in a column (separated by the `contentSheet/gap` token) inside the sheet's padding. The sheet has **no fixed height** — it grows and shrinks to fit these children automatically.

gaps.text: Open since #203 (question 6): on a phone with a home indicator the package adds the bottom safe-area inset on top of Figma's 41 px bottom padding (safeAreaBottom, on by default); whether Figma means the inset to be added is not decided.
